newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel says still hopes for debt deal end-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel says still hopes for debt deal end-Sept.

text.p: Eurotunnel said on Monday it still hoped to reach an agreement with its bank creditors on a debt restructuring by September 30.
"Our aim is still to reach an agreeement on September 30," chairman Patrick Ponsolle told reporters.

Ponsolle said there was a near-consensus on the instruments and the structure for the debt restructuring, but what remained to be agreed was the sharing of pain betweeen the bank lenders and shareholders.
"What is still being discussed is the division of pain and the hope of gains between shareholders and lenders," he said.

Earlier Eurotunnel said its accounting loss for the first half of 1996, taking into account interest due but not paid, totalled 3,043 million francs ($596.7 million), an improvement of 618 million on the same period in 1995.

Since March Eurotunnel has broken even at the operating level before financial charges and after operating expenses and investment, it said in a statement with its first half results. ($1 = 5.10 francs)
